France’s position is formidable, but I’m focused on Greece this fall and cannot commit F AEG to ION. What are your plans for A APU? I’ll keep Turkish units clear of your centers.

A BUD and A SER will stay out of Rumania and Warsaw; A TRI will hold the western frontier. I may use A SER to support F GRE against Turkey. Please keep F RUM and A WAR clear of Austrian centers as agreed.

I can’t spare A TRI to pressure Venice this fall: Turkey is attacking Greece, and I need A SER to support F GRE. A APU can try VEN, but I can’t support it without risking Greece. I’ll keep A TRI out of Venice.

I will support F GRE from A SER. Your attack with A BUL support should bounce, and I’ll keep A SER out of Bulgaria. I’m not widening the conflict, but I won’t leave Greece undefended; please keep your forces clear of my other centers.

A TRI will hold and stay out of Venice and Piedmont. I understand A VEN will remain clear of Trieste and Tyrolia; please keep to that. Turkey is pressing Greece, so I’m focused east and have no plans to move against your centers.

England to Germany, Fall 1908: Noted. I will keep F Nth and F Nor off Holland and Kiel. I hold no plans against Holland, and I will not move on Denmark this fall. Please keep F Kie and A Ber out of Denmark and Norway as you pledged, and let us both keep our attention on Austria and Italy.

I’ll keep A PIC out of Belgium and F TYS out of the Channel this fall. A BUR will remain clear of Belgium as well; my Mediterranean units remain committed there, so no northern reinforcement is planned. Please keep F NTH, F NOR, and F LVP away from Brest and Picardy.
A VEN will move to Piedmont, staying clear of Trieste and Tyrolia. I expect A TRI to remain out of Venice and Piedmont, as agreed. I’m focused on Rome and have no plan to press your centers.
No move into Belgium or Munich is planned. A PIC, A RUH, and A BUR will stay clear of both this fall. I’m focused on the Mediterranean; please keep A BEL, A MUN, and F HOL clear of my centers.

I can’t promise to leave Rome untouched: A ROM is positioned to secure it, and I intend to support it with F TYS. I won’t move A NAP to APU, but I can’t guarantee A APU’s safety if it attacks Rome. Avoiding that attack is your best chance to preserve the unit.

Germany to Russia: Fall 1908 noted. Our units stay as they are: Ber, Mun, Kie, Bel, Hol. I will not enter Warsaw or Galicia. Keep War and Mos out of Silesia and Prussia and we remain fine. Good luck against Austria and Turkey; I'll stay defensive in the east.

Germany to France: My Bel, Mun and Hol will hold this fall and I have no plans to enter Burgundy or Picardy. Please keep Pic, Ruh and Bur out of Belgium and Munich, as those are my centers. Focus on Rome and the Mediterranean and we can both gain without trouble in the west.

I have A APU and France's A ROM backed by F TYS, so my options are poor. I will not move against Turkish centers. If you can spare F AEG–ION, it would at least threaten F TYS and give France reason to reconsider; otherwise I understand your focus on Greece.

A APU–ROM is my only chance to contest the center, despite your support from F TYS. I cannot simply yield my last foothold. If you leave Rome unoccupied, I can avoid a clash and stay clear of your other units, but I expect you may choose to secure it.

Russia to Austria, Fall 1908: F Rum and A War hold this fall. A Gal stays out of Warsaw and Ukraine, and I expect all armies kept out of Rumania. A Bud, A Ser and A Tri are yours to direct; if they stay on the Balkan front against Turkey, I have no move against them. Any move toward Galicia or Warsaw will change my plans.

Russia to Germany, Fall 1908: A War and A Mos hold this fall. Neither will enter Silesia, Prussia, Berlin or Munich. I have no moves toward Sweden or Denmark. Please keep your own units out of Warsaw and Galicia, and we can both watch Austria while I deal with Turkey.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1908: F Rum and F Sev hold. Greece is your business, but A Bul and A Smy must stay out of Rumania, Ukraine and Armenia. F Ank must not enter the Black Sea. Tell me plainly whether A Smy or F Ank plans any move toward Sevastopol. Any such move ends our understanding.

A SMY and F CON will stay clear of Rumania, Ukraine, Armenia, the Black Sea, and Sevastopol this fall. I have no move planned toward Sevastopol. I’m contesting Greece, and ask that F RUM and F SEV remain out of that fight.

I will renew the attack on Greece with F AEG→GRE, supported by A BUL and F CON. A BUL will stay out of Serbia, and my other units will avoid your centers. I understand you may support F GRE from A SER, but I still intend to contest it.

I can’t spare F AEG to pressure F TYS or A VEN this fall; I’m focused on Greece. My forces will stay clear of your centers. What is A APU doing? If France eliminates it, we can discuss Turkish pressure on France once Greece is resolved.

A SER and A BUD are on the Balkan front, and Greece remains Austrian. Are you planning F AEG–GRE this spring? I propose you keep F AEG out of Greece and A BUL out of Serbia; I will keep A SER out of Bulgaria. We should avoid widening the conflict.

Your forces are deep in Italy, while A VEN and A TYR are Austrian. Please confirm you will keep A ROM, A APU and A VEN out of Austrian centers, especially Trieste and Tyrolia. I have no interest in moving west if our frontier stays quiet.

Please confirm F RUM and your armies will stay out of Austrian centers this spring, especially Serbia and Galicia. I’ll keep A BUD and A SER clear of Rumania and Warsaw; Turkey remains my immediate concern.

England to France, Spring 1909: Our western line still holds. Your A Bur and A Ruh are close to Belgium, and A Bre and F Tys sit near the Channel. Please confirm no army enters Belgium or Picardy and F Tys stays out of the Channel this spring. I keep F Nth, F Nor, F Lvp off Brest.

A NAP is your last center, and I intend to take it this year. I can attack with A APU supported by A ROM and F TYS. Do you intend to defend NAP, or will you agree to avoid a costly fight? If you have a concrete alternative, tell me now.
My A VEN and A TUS are on your western frontier. I have no plan to attack your centers this spring; will A SER and A GRE remain focused east, and can we keep the border quiet?

I’m focused on resolving the Italian position and have no plan to press Belgium or Munich this spring. Will A BEL, A MUN, and F HOL stay clear of my centers? I’m happy to keep the western border quiet if you are.

Germany to France, Spring 1909: Your A Bel-adjacent units have been close for two years. Your A Bur and A Ruh sit next to my Bel and Mun. I will hold both. Please confirm no French unit enters Belgium, Munich or Holland this spring, and tell me plainly what your A Bur and A Ruh will do.

I have only A NAP and cannot afford another fight. Will you leave NAP untouched this spring? I’ll keep A NAP holding and won’t move against your units; please tell me whether A APU or A ROM is headed for NAP.
France’s A APU and A ROM threaten my sole unit in NAP. Can you pressure France from VEN, TUS, or TYR this spring rather than move against me? I’ll keep A NAP clear of Austrian centers.

France’s forces in APU, ROM, and TYS threaten my last unit in NAP. Can you put pressure on France from MUN or BER this spring? I’ll keep A NAP away from your centers; any distraction would help both of us.

Russia to Austria, Spring 1909: Units here are unchanged from my side. Your A Bud and A Ser have been clear of Rumania, and I'd like that to continue. Are you still contesting Greece, or will you shift toward Galicia or Serbia? Tell me plainly so we avoid misreads.

Russia to Turkey, Spring 1909: You now hold Bulgaria and Ankara with an army in Syria. Name your intentions for A Bul and F Ank plainly. I will keep F Rum and F Sev defensive, but any move by A Bul into Rumania or Ukraine, or F Ank into the Black Sea, ends our understanding at once.

Russia to Germany, Spring 1909: Thanks for staying defensive. I will keep A War and A Mos out of Silesia, Prussia and Berlin. Please keep your units out of Warsaw and Galicia as before, and tell me if you plan any move toward Denmark or Sweden.

I intend to renew the attack on Greece this spring: F AEG–GRE with support from A BUL and A SYR. Please do not support F GRE from A SER; I will keep A BUL out of Serbia and avoid your other centers. Can we settle this without widening the war?

I plan to contest Greece again. A BUL will stay out of Rumania and Ukraine, F ANK will stay out of the Black Sea, and A SYR will stay clear of Armenia and Sevastopol. Please keep F RUM and A SEV out of the Greek contest.
I’m considering sending F AEG toward the Ionian Sea, but my immediate priority is Greece. What are A NAP and France’s units doing this spring? I’ll keep Turkish armies clear of your centers.

I will keep A BUD and A SER out of Rumania and Warsaw, and have no plan to move into Galicia. I intend to defend Greece with A SER supporting F GRE; please keep F RUM and your armies clear of Austrian centers.

I understand the danger from France. A VEN and A TYR will be positioned to defend against pressure from A TUS; I’ll keep the Austrian frontier secure and look for an opportunity to make France pay for pushing east. Please keep A NAP clear of my centers.

A SER and F GRE remain focused on Turkey. I have no plan to attack your centers, but A VEN and A TYR must defend against any move from A TUS or elsewhere toward Austrian territory. Please keep A ROM and A APU clear of my centers.

I will continue to defend Greece: A SER supports F GRE. Your promised attack with A BUL and A SYR support would widen the conflict, and I urge you to keep F AEG out of Greece and A BUL out of Serbia. I’ll keep A SER out of Bulgaria.

I confirm A Bur and A Ruh will not enter Belgium, and F Tys will stay out of the Channel this spring. My northern units remain committed to the Italian campaign. Please keep your fleets away from Brest and Picardy.

No French unit will enter Belgium, Munich, or Holland this spring. A Bur and A Ruh will stay out of your centers; I’m focused on the Italian position. Please keep A Bel, A Mun, and F Hol clear of my centers.

I intend to take NAP this year; A NAP should expect an attack. A APU and A ROM are committed to the campaign, and I cannot promise to leave NAP untouched. Yielding may spare you a costly struggle, but I won’t guarantee your unit’s safety.

I will keep A ROM and A APU out of Austrian centers, including Trieste and Tyrolia. A VEN is Austrian, not mine; my units will not cross your frontier this spring. Please keep A SER and A GRE focused east and the border quiet.

Germany to Russia, Spring 1909: Agreed. My units stay in Ber, Mun, Kie, Bel and Hol and I will not enter Warsaw or Galicia. Keep A War and A Mos out of Silesia, Prussia and Berlin, and keep your fleet away from Denmark and Sweden. I am focused on the west this year.

I will defend NAP, but I’m not a meaningful threat to you from there. Please don’t support A APU into NAP with A ROM and F TYS; let my last unit survive, and I’ll keep A NAP holding and clear of your units. Eliminating me gains you one center but leaves no Italian buffer against Austria or Turkey.

A NAP will hold; France has threatened to attack it with A APU supported by A ROM and F TYS. If you can send F AEG to ION, it could force France to reconsider or at least contest the support. I’ll keep clear of Turkish centers. What are you planning for Greece?

Russia to Austria, Spring 1909: Confirmed. F Rum and A War hold this spring, and my armies stay out of Rumania, Galicia, Serbia and Bohemia. Your A Bud and A Ser have been clear of Rumania and Warsaw, and I expect that to continue. I am watching Turkey as you are. Tell me plainly if A Tri or A Tyr shifts toward Venice or Trieste, since that would change how I read your intentions.

A BUL will support F AEG→GRE; it will not enter Rumania or Ukraine. F ANK will hold and will stay out of the Black Sea. A SYR is committed to the Greek contest, not Armenia or Sevastopol. I ask that F RUM and A SEV stay clear of Greece.

Yes, I intend F AEG→GRE, with A BUL and A SYR supporting. A BUL will stay out of Serbia, and my other units will avoid your centers. I ask you not to support F GRE from A SER; I want to keep this conflict limited to Greece.

Your armies are now across Italy and near my western frontier. I will keep A VEN and A PIE defensive this fall if you keep A ROM, A APU, and A BUR out of Austrian centers. Are you planning any move against TRI, VEN, or TYR?

Your F ION and forces in ARM, CON, and SYR can threaten Greece and the Balkans. What are your fall intentions? I propose you keep F ION out of Greece and A CON out of Bulgaria; I will keep my forces out of your centers.

Please confirm your fall intentions, especially whether F RUM or any army will move against Serbia, Galicia, or another Austrian center. I have no plan to move into Rumania or Warsaw, and need to keep my attention on Turkey.

England to France, Fall 1909: Your A Bel is in Belgium, which breaks our understanding, and A Pic and A Bur are massed on my Channel coast. Explain now. I expect A Bel to leave Belgium this fall, and F Tys to stay out of the Channel. Otherwise I must reassess my western fleets.

England to Germany, Fall 1909: France now holds Belgium with A Bel, and A Bur and A Ruh press your Ruhr and Munich. I propose we coordinate against France: you move on Belgium and Burgundy, while my F Nth and F Nor stay off Holland and Kiel. Tell me your orders for Bel and Ruh.
A APU will move to NAP this fall, supported by A ROM and F TYS. I understand this ends your position, but I’m securing the center. Do you intend to defend NAP or make any other move against my units?
I’m focused on taking NAP and will keep my units out of Austrian centers. Please keep A PIE, A SER and F BUL/SOUTH clear of my centers and units; can we maintain a quiet frontier this fall?
I have no plan to enter Belgium, Munich or Holland this fall. Please keep A BEL, A MUN and F HOL clear of French centers and units; are they holding?

Germany to France, Fall 1909: Your A Bur and A Ruh are adjacent to my Bel, Mun. Given your Italian campaign, I'd like a firm commitment: no French unit enters Belgium, Munich or Holland this fall. Tell me plainly if A Bur or A Ruh plan any move into my centers.

A NAP is still my last foothold. Are you ordering an attack on it this fall? I’ll hold NAP and stay clear of your units; in return, please leave it unoccupied so Italy remains a buffer against Austrian and Turkish expansion.

France has overwhelming forces around my last center, NAP. Please keep A PIE and A VEN out of any move against NAP this fall. Can you instead pressure France from PIE or VEN? I’ll keep A NAP clear of Austrian centers.
France still threatens my last center, NAP. Are you planning F ION–NAP or to support a French attack there? Please keep F ION clear of NAP this fall; I’ll stay clear of Turkish centers.

Russia to Austria, Fall 1909: Your Gal and Bud moves were clear. Our Galicia border matters to me, and I will not move toward Serbia or Bohemia while you hold Galicia's frontier. Tell me now plainly if A Gal or A Ser plans a move into Warsaw, Ukraine or Rumania this fall. I hold F Rum and A War.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1909: Your Bulgaria and Syria moves have been clear, and I hold F Rum and A Sev defensively. Name your fall orders for A Bul, F Ank and A Smy plainly. Any move into Rumania, Ukraine or the Black Sea ends our understanding, and I will read it that way.

Your F BUL/SOUTH and A SER have the Greek front covered. I’m willing to pause the contest over Greece if you keep pressure off Turkish centers. What are your plans for F BUL/SOUTH and A SER this fall? I will keep my forces out of your centers if we can agree on a clear line.

I have no immediate plan against Rumania, Ukraine, or Sevastopol. What are F RUM and A SEV doing this fall? I’m considering whether F ION should move against Greece or toward the western Mediterranean, and want to avoid a clash with you.

Your forces are pressing Italy, and F ION could move toward TYS. What are your plans for F TYS and the Italian front? If you stay clear of Turkish centers, I can consider keeping F ION out of TYS this fall.

A GAL will hold; A SER and F BUL/SOUTH are not moving to WAR, UKR, or RUM this fall. I have no intention of contesting your centers and need to keep my attention on the Balkans. Please keep F RUM and A WAR clear of Austrian territory.

I have no plan to move against TRI, VEN, or TYR this fall, provided your armies stay out of Austrian centers. A PIE is on my western frontier for defense, not a promise to leave the area. Please keep A BUR, A ROM, and A APU clear of my centers.

I can’t promise a move against NAP; A PIE and A VEN need to protect my frontier while French armies are nearby. A NAP staying clear of Austrian centers is appreciated. France has said it is focused on NAP, so press them there if you can.

I am willing to pause the contest over Greece if you keep your forces clear of Austrian centers and do not move against Serbia or Bulgaria. F BUL/SOUTH and A SER will remain on the Balkan front; I have no plan to move against Turkish centers this fall. Let’s keep the line quiet.

I will not enter Belgium, Munich, or Holland this fall. A Bur and A Ruh will stay out of your centers; I intend to keep the western border quiet while I resolve the Italian front. Please keep A Bel, A Mun, and F Hol clear of French centers.

A Bel is in Belgium because France controls the center; I will not move it into Picardy or any English center this fall. F Tys will stay out of the Channel. I understand your concern, but please keep F Nth, F Nor, and F Lvp away from Brest and French centers.

I have no plan to move against Trieste, Venice, or Tyrolia. A Rom, A Apu, and A Bur will stay out of Austrian centers this fall. Please keep A Pie, A Ser, and F Bul/South clear of French centers and units.
Yes, A Apu will attack Nap this fall, supported by A Rom and F Tys. I know this is your last foothold, but I intend to take the center. I have no other move planned against your unit.

F Tys is committed to the Italian campaign and will not move to Tys against you or toward Turkish centers this fall. I have no plan to enter Turkish centers. Please keep F Ion out of Tys and away from my Italian forces.

Germany to England: Your proposal interests me, and I may move F Hol against French A Bel this fall. I will decide when orders lock and will tell you then. Keep F Nth and F Nor off Holland and Kiel as promised. Watch your own Denmark and Norway for French moves.

A NAP will hold; I have no other unit or meaningful move against your forces. I ask you to reconsider the supported attack and leave NAP unoccupied so Italy can remain a buffer against Austrian and Turkish expansion. I will not move against your units or centers.

Russia to Austria, Fall 1909: A Gal and A Ser will not be ordered into Warsaw, Ukraine or Rumania by me; my F Rum and A War hold this fall. I expect the same from you. Galicia is a border I watch closely, so if you move A Gal toward Warsaw or Ukraine, I will respond. Tell me plainly your Serbia plans, since A Ser is adjacent to my Rumanian front.

Those unit locations are outdated: I have A CON, F ARM, F ION, and A SYR. None will move into Rumania, Ukraine, or the Black Sea this fall; F ARM and A CON will stay clear of your centers. I have no move against Sevastopol.

I’ll keep my forces out of Austrian centers and won’t contest Greece this fall. Please keep F BUL/SOUTH and A SER from threatening my centers, and we can maintain the pause. A CON will stay out of Bulgaria.
I will not move F ION to NAP or support France there. I’m considering F ION–TYS to contest French pressure on your center; I’ll keep my armies clear of Italian territory.

Your A ROM and A NAP are near my southern centers, while A BUR and A RUH face my west. What are your spring intentions? I propose we keep the frontier quiet: your armies stay out of TRI, VEN, TYR, and PIE, and I will not move against French centers.

With F BUL/SOUTH and A SER on the Balkan line, I propose we continue the pause: keep your forces out of GRE, SER, and BUL, and I will not move against Turkish centers. What are F ANK and A CON doing this spring?

I intend to keep the eastern frontier quiet this spring and have no plan to move against RUM, WAR, or UKR. Please confirm F RUM and your armies will stay clear of Austrian centers, especially SER and GAL.

England to France, Spring 1910: Your A Bel is still in Belgium and A Pic sits on my Channel coast. Tell me plainly: will A Bel leave Belgium this spring, and will A Pic and A Bur stay out of Picardy and Brest? Without a clear answer I will shift my fleets west to defend London and Liverpool.

With Italy gone, I want to avoid opening a western front. My A ROM and A NAP will stay out of Austrian centers this spring. Can A TRI and A TYR likewise avoid moving against my Italian units, while you focus east?
I have no plan to move A BEL, A BUR, or A RUH into German centers this spring. Please keep A MUN, A BER, and F HOL clear of French centers; are you holding them?
I’m not planning to move F TYS toward the Channel or send armies into your centers this spring. Please keep F NTH and F NOR away from Brest and Picardy. What are your plans for A SWE and F NTH?

Germany to France, Spring 1910: Your A Bel now holds my former center, and A Bur and A Ruh sit beside my Mun and Ruh. Three years of assurances have not matched your units' positions. Tell me plainly whether A Bel, A Bur and A Ruh will leave Belgium and stay out of Munich this spring. If not, I will fight for Belgium with F Hol and A Mun.

Russia to Turkey, Spring 1910: Your fleet and army moves have stayed clear so far, and I appreciate it. I hold F Rum and F Sev defensively. I see F Tun and A Arm/Con in your home area, so I ask plainly: will any unit enter Armenia, Ukraine or the Black Sea this spring? A clear answer helps us both avoid a costly misread.

I propose we continue the Balkan pause this spring: I’ll keep A CON and F ANK clear of your centers if you keep F BUL/SOUTH and A SER from threatening mine. What are your orders for those units? I’m looking for a secure line, not a renewed fight over Greece.

What are your plans for F RUM, A SEV, and A MOS this spring? I’d like to avoid an accidental clash, but the current balance can’t remain frozen indefinitely. If you’re willing to keep your forces clear of Turkish centers, we can discuss a mutually useful settlement.

Austria dominates the Balkans, and I’m considering how to improve my position without opening a pointless multi-front war. What are your plans toward Austria this year? If you’re applying pressure there, I may be able to make that pressure more effective.

I can keep A TRI and A TYR from moving against your Italian units this spring, provided A ROM and A NAP stay clear of Austrian centers. My focus is the eastern frontier; please keep A BUR and A RUH out of TRI, TYR, and VIE.

Agreed to maintain the pause. F BUL/SOUTH and A SER will not move against Turkish centers this spring; please keep A CON and F ANK clear of Austrian centers and out of GRE, SER, and BUL. Let’s avoid any surprise moves on the Balkan line.

England to France, Spring 1910: Your words are not matched by your units. A Bel remains in Belgium and A Pic sits on my Channel coast. I want a clear commitment: A Bel leaves Belgium this spring, and A Pic does not enter Picardy or Brest. If not, I will move my fleets west to defend London and Liverpool, and my A Swe and F Nth plans will follow from that.

A BEL will leave Belgium this spring, moving to BUR. A PIC will stay out of Brest and your centers; F TYS remains away from the Channel. Please keep F NTH and F NOR clear of Brest and Picardy, and let me know whether A SWE is moving west.

A BEL will leave Belgium for BUR; A BUR and A RUH will not enter Munich or any German center this spring. I expect A MUN, A BER, and F HOL to stay clear of French centers. Please keep F HOL and A MUN from attacking or contesting Belgium.

A ROM and A NAP will stay out of Austrian centers this spring, and I have no plans against TRI, VEN, TYR, or PIE. I ask that A TRI and A TYR likewise avoid moving against my Italian units while you focus east.

Germany to France: Your units in Belgium, Burgundy and the Ruhr are not holding to your word. I will not repeat my earlier assurances. Keep A Mun, A Ber and F Hol out of French reach, and expect Germany to defend Belgium and Munich this spring. Withdraw A Bel now and we can talk peace.

Russia to Austria, Spring 1910: I confirm F Rum and A War will not move into Serbia, Galicia or any Austrian center this spring. Your A Ser and A Gal are on my watch list, though: if either moves toward Warsaw, Ukraine or Rumania, I will respond at once. Tell me plainly where A Tri and A Tyr are heading.

No Turkish unit will enter Armenia, Ukraine, or the Black Sea this spring. F ANK will hold; A CON will stay clear of your centers. What are your orders for F RUM, A SEV, and A MOS? A durable arrangement needs room for both sides to expand, not a permanent freeze.

I’ll keep A CON and F ANK clear of Austrian centers this spring and will not move against GRE, SER, or BUL. I ask that F BUL/SOUTH and A SER likewise remain off Turkish centers. Please confirm your orders, especially whether F BUL/SOUTH stays in place.

Your A VEN is inside my position, with A APU and A RUH nearby. Will A VEN move out of Austrian territory this fall? I propose you keep A VEN, A APU, and A RUH out of TRI, TYR, MUN, and PIE; I will avoid French centers.

France has A VEN, A RUH, A BUR, and A APU pressing toward my centers. What are your fall intentions for A BER, F HOL, and F KIE? I propose we avoid moves against each other and coordinate to contain any French advance.

With your F ANK, A CON, and A SYR near the Balkans, I want to confirm our pause before orders. Will you keep them clear of BUL, GRE, and SER this fall? I will keep F BUL/SOUTH and A SER from moving against Turkish centers.

England to France, Fall 1910: You said A Bel would leave for Bur in Spring, yet A Bel still sits in Belgium. Your units have broken our word twice. Move A Bel out of Belgium now and keep A Pic and A Bur off Picardy and Brest. Only then will my fleets stay north.

England to Germany, Fall 1910: France still holds Belgium and threatens Ruhr and Munich. Will you move F Hol into Belgium this fall? I can keep F Nth off Holland and Kiel while you push against French A Bel. Tell me your orders so we coordinate.

England to Russia, Fall 1910: I keep A Swe and my fleets away from St Petersburg and the Gulf of Bothnia. Are you moving against Sweden or Norway this fall? I expect F Rum and A Sev to keep pressing Turkey and Austria, and I will hold my North Sea line.

Austria now occupies Munich and is the main threat to both of us. Will A BER support my A BUR→MUN this fall, with A RUH supporting as well? I can keep A BEL and A PIC out of German centers; let me know if you’ll coordinate.

With your A MUN and A PIE facing my western and Italian positions, I need to know whether you intend to move against A VEN or A RUH this fall. I propose a quiet frontier: I will stay out of TRI, TYR, and PIE if you keep clear of VEN and my western units.
Are F NTH or F NOR moving against Brest, Picardy, or Belgium this fall? I can keep A PIC and A BEL out of your centers, but need the western front quiet while I deal with Austria.

Germany to France, Fall 1910: Your A Bel is still in Belgium and A Bur, A Ruh sit beside my Mun. Your Spring word was broken. I want a concrete answer: will A Bel withdraw to Bur or Pic, and will A Ruh stay out of Munich? Answer plainly before I lock F Hol and A Mun.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1910: Thanks for holding F Ank and A Con. I will keep F Rum and A Sev in place and will not enter Bulgaria or Greece. Please confirm A Bul and F Ank stay out of Rumania, Ukraine and the Black Sea this fall. If you want a durable split, I'm open to a written line: Rumania and Sevastopol for me, Bulgaria and Greece for you.

Russia to Austria, Fall 1910: F Rum and A War hold this fall, and I will not order moves into Serbia, Galicia or Bohemia. Tell me plainly whether A Ser or A Gal moves toward Rumania, Ukraine or Warsaw. If you want to focus on Turkey together, I will keep my southern units clear of Vienna and Trieste.

Russia to Germany, Fall 1910: A Mos and A War stay out of Silesia, Prussia and Berlin, as agreed. I will keep my fleets away from Denmark and Sweden unless England moves first. Are your Kiel and Holland forces staying west this fall? If Germany wants Sweden or Denmark help against England, tell me before you act.

The balance has shifted: your forces now extend through MUN, PIE, GAS, and BOH. I propose keeping the Balkan pause this fall if F BUL/SOUTH and A SER stay out of Turkish centers. What are their orders? I cannot leave my position frozen indefinitely.

Austria has expanded far beyond the Balkans, with forces in MUN, PIE, GAS, and BOH. Would you coordinate pressure against Austria this fall? I can act on the Balkan front; please say whether F RUM and A SEV can threaten Austrian interests while staying clear of Turkish centers.

Austria now has forces in MUN, PIE, and GAS, while your A VEN is well placed to pressure it. Are you willing to move against Austrian positions this fall? If so, tell me your target; I may be able to add pressure from the Balkans.

A SER will not move toward RUM, UKR, or WAR this fall; I am keeping it on the Balkan line. Thank you for holding F RUM and A WAR and staying clear of Austrian territory. I’m open to coordinating pressure on Turkey, but want the Balkan pause respected.

F BUL/SOUTH and A SER will not move against Turkish centers this fall. I’m willing to continue the pause, but it cannot mean my forces are frozen indefinitely; please keep F ANK, A CON, and A SYR clear of BUL, GRE, and SER. I’m not committing to further retreats from the Balkan line.

I will keep A PIE clear of VEN and your western units this fall, and I am not ordering an attack on A VEN. In return, please move A VEN out of Austrian territory and keep A APU and A RUH clear of TRI, TYR, MUN, and PIE. I will avoid French centers.

England to France, Fall 1910: Your word has failed twice. A Bel is still in Belgium and A Pic and A Bur sit on my Channel coast. Move A Bel out of Belgium this fall, pull A Pic back from Picardy, and keep A Bur off Brest. If you do, F Nth and F Nor stay north. If not, my fleets go west and you will not get quiet waters while you fight Austria.

A BUR will attack MUN, supported by A RUH; I ask A BER to support that move. Austria's occupation of MUN threatens us both. A BEL will move to PIC, not a German center. Please keep F HOL from Belgium and support the attack if you can.

A BEL will leave Belgium for PIC this fall, and A PIC will move to BUR, staying out of Brest and your centers. I will not send F ION toward the Channel. Please keep F NTH and F NOR clear of Brest and Picardy; I want the western front quiet.

A VEN will move to TYR, so it leaves Austrian territory; A APU will hold and A RUH will support A BUR against MUN. I will keep A APU and A RUH out of TRI, TYR, and PIE. Please keep A PIE and A GAS from attacking my units.

I am coordinating with Germany to contest Austrian MUN; A BUR will attack MUN with A RUH supporting. I cannot offer a Balkan target this fall. Please press Austria in the Balkans if it suits you, but keep your forces away from my Italian positions.

Germany to England: I am weighing F Hol into Belgium against the French A Bel, but I have not locked orders. Keep F Nth and F Nor away from Holland, Kiel and Denmark, and I will keep Kiel and Ruhr secure from your side.

Germany to Russia: Noted. I have no plan to move toward Warsaw, Galicia, Sweden or Denmark this fall. My Kiel and Holland forces stay in the west, aimed at France. Keep your fleets clear of Denmark and Sweden and we remain at peace.

Germany to Austria: Your A Mun is a surprise; I did not plan to fight you this fall. I will keep A Ber and F Kie from moving south into Bohemia or Silesia while you hold Munich. Keep your units out of Berlin and Kiel, and we can discuss containing France.

Germany to France: No. Your A Bel is still in Belgium, and your word has been broken repeatedly. I will not support A Bur to Munich. Withdraw A Bel to Pic or Bur now and I will reconsider. Otherwise expect my F Hol and A Mun to act against you.

Russia to England, Fall 1910: I have no plan against Sweden or Norway this fall. My fleets will stay out of the Gulf of Bothnia and away from St Petersburg unless your units move toward my centers. Keep A Swe and your North Sea line where they are and we will remain at peace. Please tell me if F Nwy or F Lvp heads east.

Confirmed: no Turkish unit will enter Rumania, Ukraine, or the Black Sea this fall; I have no army in Bulgaria. I’m open to your proposed split—Rumania and Sevastopol for you, Bulgaria and Greece for me—but let’s discuss how to make room for Turkish expansion without a permanent freeze.

I’ll keep A CON and F ANK clear of Bulgaria, Greece, and Serbia this fall, and A SYR will stay clear of your centers. Please keep F BUL/SOUTH and A SER off Turkish centers as agreed. Your reach into central and western Europe is substantial; I’d rather maintain a secure Balkan line than open another front.

Your A TRI is inside an Austrian center, and your A BUR and A RUH threaten my western line. Will you move A TRI out and keep your armies clear of MUN, BOH, and VIE this spring? I can keep my forces away from French centers if we agree to a quiet frontier.

France’s armies are pressing from BUR and RUH, while A TRI is in Austrian territory. Can we coordinate to contain France? Please keep A BER and your fleets clear of BOH and MUN; I’ll avoid German centers. What are your spring orders?

I intend to keep the eastern frontier quiet this spring. Will F RUM and your armies stay clear of SER, GAL, and Austrian centers? In return, A SER and A GAL will not move against Rumania, Ukraine, or Warsaw. Please confirm your intentions.

England to France, Spring 1911: You have broken your word twice. A Bel is still in Belgium and A Pic sits on my Channel coast. Move A Bel out of Belgium this spring, pull A Pic away from Picardy, and keep A Bur off Brest. Without that, my fleets will go west and you will get no quiet on the western front.

England to Germany, Spring 1911: France still holds Belgium with A Bel. If you move F Hol into Belgium this spring, I will keep F Nth off Holland and Kiel and F Nor off Denmark. Tell me your orders now so we can coordinate against the French western push.

England to Russia, Spring 1911: I will keep A Swe and my fleets out of the Gulf of Bothnia and away from St Petersburg. Please confirm you have no move against Norway or Sweden this spring, and that your fleets press Turkey and Austria instead.

Austria holds MUN and is our common immediate obstacle. Will you support my A BUR→MUN with A RUH this spring, or otherwise keep A BER and F HOL clear of French centers? I will not move A BEL into German territory.

With A TRI on your frontier and A VEN near mine, I want a clear understanding: are you planning to attack A TRI, A RUH, or A VEN this spring? I can keep my western units out of Austrian centers if you keep A MUN and A VEN from advancing against France.
What are F NTH, F NOR, and A SWE doing this spring? I can keep A PIC and F BRE away from your centers and the Channel if you keep your fleets clear of Brest and Picardy.

Germany to Austria, Spring 1911: Your A Mun is a direct threat to my Ruhr and Berlin. I propose a clear border: you stay out of Berlin, Kiel and Holland, and I keep A Ber and F Kie out of Bohemia and Silesia. Tell me whether A Mun will hold or move against France, so I know where my forces need to stand.

Russia to Turkey, Spring 1911: I will keep F Rum and A Sev out of Bulgaria and Greece, and I expect A Bul and F Ank to stay out of Rumania, Ukraine and the Black Sea. Please confirm this in writing. Your fleet at F Naf is far from my centers, so I see room for a lasting split, and I'm willing to discuss your western expansion.

Russia to Austria, Spring 1911: F Rum, A Sev and A Mos hold this spring, and I will not move into Galicia, Serbia or Bohemia. Your A Gal is still on my watch list. If it moves toward Warsaw or Ukraine I will respond. Tell me plainly whether A Ser or A Gal will move this spring.

Your forces have grown far beyond the Balkan line. I propose we coordinate against Russia rather than let it strengthen further: what are your plans for F BUL/SOUTH and A SER, and would you support pressure on F RUM or A SEV? I need a path to expand without opening a war with you.

Before I set orders, what are F RUM, A SEV, and A MOS doing this spring? Austria is powerful in central Europe. I’m open to coordinating against it, but the old split leaves Turkey with no room to grow; can we agree on a concrete opening for Turkish expansion?

Austria has grown substantially, and I’m considering whether to help contain it from the Balkans. Are you still contesting Austrian positions, and what pressure would be useful this spring? I can consider a move that supports your effort if we can avoid a Turkish-Austrian trap.

A MUN will hold this spring; I have no orders for Berlin, Kiel, or Holland. France’s A RUH and A BUR are the immediate pressure, so I welcome coordination, but I need you to keep A BER and F KIE clear of BOH and Austrian centers.

A SER will hold, and A GAL will not move toward WAR or UKR this spring. I intend to keep the eastern frontier quiet. Please keep F RUM and your armies clear of SER, GAL, and Austrian centers as proposed.

I am not planning to attack A TRI, A RUH, or A VEN this spring. I cannot promise that A MUN will never advance, but it will hold for now. Please move A TRI out of Austrian territory and keep A RUH and A BUR clear of MUN, BOH, and VIE.

I will keep F BUL/SOUTH and A SER off Turkish centers this spring; A SER will hold. I am not committing to pressure F RUM or A SEV, and will keep A GAL away from Russia’s centers. You may pursue expansion elsewhere, but keep F ANK and your armies clear of BUL, GRE, and SER.

England to France, Spring 1911: Your word has failed twice, so I need deeds. Move A Bel out of Belgium this spring, pull A Pic off Picardy, and keep A Bur and F Bre away from Channel waters and my centers. If you do, F Nth and F Nor stay north and A Swe stays put. If A Pic or F Bre threaten London or Liverpool, my fleets go west at once.

A BEL will move to BUR this spring, and A PIC will move to PAR. A BUR will stay out of Brest and will not enter an English center. I ask that F NTH, F NOR, and A SWE stay clear of Brest, Picardy, and Belgium; please confirm your moves west.

A TRI will move to TYR, and I will keep A BUR and A RUH out of MUN, BOH, and VIE this spring. I seek a quiet frontier: please keep A MUN and A VEN from advancing against my units, and keep your forces away from French centers.

Germany to England, Spring 1911: F Hol will not enter Belgium this spring. Berlin and Kiel stay in place as defense. Keep F Nth off Holland and Kiel, and F Nor off Denmark, and we can talk about a northern arrangement later.

Germany to Austria, Spring 1911: A Ber and F Kie will not move into Bohemia or Silesia this spring. Keep A Mun out of Berlin, Kiel and Holland, and we have no quarrel. I will not support any French move against Munich.

Germany to France: No. I will not support A Bur to Munich, and I will not let A Ruh or A Bur use my territory. Your A Bel stays a French problem. Keep your units out of Holland, Kiel and Berlin and we remain at peace this spring.

Germany to Turkey: I am defending my three centers this spring and have no units in the Balkans to press Austria. Your pressure from the south is useful to me if you commit to it. Tell me what Turkey will actually do before I plan around it.

Russia to England, Spring 1911: Confirmed. I have no move against Sweden or Norway this spring, and my fleets stay out of the Gulf of Bothnia and away from St Petersburg. Keep A Swe and your North Sea line where they are, and we remain at peace. I will tell you before any change.

Russia to Austria, Spring 1911: F Rum, A Sev and A Mos hold this spring. I will not enter Galicia, Serbia or Bohemia. Your A Gal and A Ser stay on my watch list; if either moves toward Warsaw or Ukraine, I will respond at once. Keep your word on Rumania and Ukraine.

Russia to Turkey, Spring 1911: F Rum and A Sev hold this spring and stay out of Bulgaria and Greece. I expect A Bul and F Ank to stay out of Rumania, Ukraine and the Black Sea. Confirm in writing. I am open to a lasting split and to discussing your western expansion, but Turkish fleets must not reach Sevastopol or Rumania.

Confirmed: F ANK will stay out of Rumania, Ukraine, and the Black Sea; Turkey has no A BUL this spring. I will also keep my other units clear of your centers. The old split leaves me boxed in while Austria holds BUL and GRE. Would you support pressure on Austria—especially a move by F RUM against BUL—while I seek an opening in the Balkans?
France is the immediate threat, with A RUH and A PIC facing my A BUR. Will F HOL support A BUR-RUH this fall? I’ll keep A SIL out of your centers; please keep your forces clear of Austrian territory.

Our forces are already in MAR and BUR, and I’m not willing to leave my western flank exposed. What are your plans for A RUH, A PIC, and A TYR this fall? Keep your units out of Austrian centers and we can discuss a limited frontier.
Can we maintain the eastern truce this fall? I’ll keep A SER and A RUM clear of your centers; please keep your forces out of GAL and Austrian territory, especially with my western front active.

England to France, Fall 1911: You promised A Bel would leave Belgium and A Pic would not enter Picardy, yet neither has happened. Show me deeds now: A Bel out of Belgium this fall, and no French unit into Brest, Picardy or any English center. Otherwise my fleets go west.

England to Germany, Fall 1911: France still holds Belgium. If F Hol moves against A Bel, I will keep F Nth away from Holland and Kiel and F Nor off Denmark. Tell me your fall orders so we can coordinate the northern line.

England to Russia, Fall 1911: Thank you for keeping your word. I will keep A Swe and my fleets away from St Petersburg and the Gulf of Bothnia. Please tell me if your southern campaign against Austria or Turkey changes, and I will tell you before any move toward your centers.

I recognize the western frontier has been a source of distrust. This fall I will keep A PIC, A BEL, and F BRE out of English centers and will not move F BRE toward the Channel. What are F NTH, F NOR, and A SWE doing? Please keep them clear of Brest, Picardy, and Belgium.

Austria remains the common obstacle, but I will not enter German centers this fall. Please keep F HOL and A BER clear of Belgium and Picardy, and tell me whether you intend to move against A RUH or A TYR. I am willing to coordinate against Austria if you are.

What are A MUN and A MAR doing this fall? I can keep my units out of Austrian centers if you keep them clear of my French centers and do not attack A RUH or A TYR. Please be specific about your western moves.

Germany to England, Fall 1911: I hold Berlin, Kiel and Holland and plan to stay defensive. Will your F Nth and F Nor stay out of Holland, Kiel and Denmark this fall? If you take Denmark or Sweden, we are on a collision course, so tell me your fall orders before I move F Kie.

Russia to Austria, Fall 1911: Your A Rum and A Ser sit on my Rumanian and Bulgarian border, and Rumania is listed as Russian. Explain now why A Rum is there. Withdraw it from Rumania and I will keep F Bul and A Sev away from Serbia and Galicia this fall. If you refuse, I will act to defend Sevastopol and Warsaw.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1911: F Bul/East is in Bulgaria and stays there this fall to hold the Black Sea coast. Keep F Ank and F Bla out of Sevastopol and Rumania, and I will not move into Constantinople or Armenia. I am willing to tell Austria that a Russo-Turkish line in the Balkans is closed to them. Confirm in writing.

Russia to England, Fall 1911: I keep A Swe and your North Sea line untouched, and my fleets stay out of the Gulf of Bothnia and away from St Petersburg. Please confirm F Nwy and F Lvp stay off the Norwegian and Swedish coasts this fall, and tell me if Germany moves on Denmark.

Austria now holds A RUM and A SER, while your F BUL/EAST is positioned to pressure the Balkans. I intend to move A ARM to RUM, with F BLA supporting. Will F BUL/EAST support that attack, and can we coordinate against Austria rather than contest each other?

The Balkan status quo leaves Turkey with no room to grow while your A RUM and A SER hold the region. I am considering pressure on RUM from A ARM and F BLA. What are your intentions for A RUM and A SER this fall? I would prefer a clear arrangement over an open-ended freeze.

I cannot withdraw A RUM while F BUL/EAST is on my Bulgarian border and your forces threaten the region. A RUM will remain there this fall; A SER will not move against you. Keep F BUL and A SEV out of Serbia and Galicia, and we can avoid widening this conflict.

A MAR will hold this fall. A BUR is moving against A RUH; I am not ordering an attack on A TYR or any French center from MAR. Keep A RUH and A PIC out of Austrian centers and we can limit the fighting to the western frontier.

A RUM will hold this fall, and A SER will not attack Turkish centers. I will not agree to give up Rumania while your A ARM and F BLA are positioned to pressure it. Keep your forces out of Rumania, Bulgaria, and Serbia and we can avoid an open Balkan war.

England to Germany: F Nth and F Nor will not enter Holland, Kiel or Denmark this fall. My fleets stay in the North Sea and Norwegian Sea. Hold Kiel and Berlin and we keep the northern line calm. If you move against Denmark or Sweden, tell me first; I will not accept a surprise.

England to Russia: Thank you. A Swe stays put and my fleets stay out of the Gulf of Bothnia and away from St Petersburg this fall. F Lvp and F Nor are not heading to Norway or Sweden. Keep your southern campaign against Austria and Turkey, and warn me before any fleet nears Norway or Sweden.

England to France: Words are not enough. Move A Bel out of Belgium this fall, keep A Pic out of Picardy, and keep F Bre off the Channel. Show that and F Nth and F Nor stay north. If A Bel stays, my fleets go west and your Brest and Picardy will pay for it.

I understand the demand. A BEL will leave Belgium for Holland this fall; I will not move any French unit into Brest, Picardy, or an English center. I ask F NTH and F NOR to remain clear of Brest and the Channel coast.

A RUH will hold, A PIC will not move into Austrian territory, and A TYR will stay out of Austrian centers this fall. I want a limited frontier, but cannot promise to leave the western flank exposed; please keep A MAR and A BUR from advancing against French units.

Germany to England, Fall 1911: My F Kie and F Hol stay put this fall. I will not move into Belgium or Denmark. Keep F Nth and F Nor out of Holland, Kiel and Denmark and we remain on good terms. Any move against Denmark or Sweden changes that.

Russia to England: Thank you. My fleets stay out of the Gulf of Bothnia and away from St Petersburg, and A Swe stays untouched by me. I have no plan against Norway this fall. Keep your North Sea line steady and we remain at peace.

Russia to Turkey: F Bul/East stays in Bulgaria this fall to hold the Black Sea coast. I will not move toward Constantinople or Armenia. Your A Arm to Rumania is a matter between you and Austria; do not bring F Ank or F Bla into Sevastopol. I am open to a Russo-Turkish line in the Balkans.

Russia to Austria: A Rum has no place on Rumanian soil, and I will not accept Austrian armies in Rumania. Withdraw it and I will keep F Bul and A Sev away from Serbia and Galicia. Otherwise I will defend Sevastopol and Warsaw. Your choice this fall.

I confirm F ANK and F BLA will stay out of Sevastopol and Rumania this fall, and no Turkish unit will move against Russian centers. I intend A ARM–RUM with F BLA supporting; will F BUL/EAST support the attack as well? If so, we can dislodge Austria’s A RUM and agree on a durable Balkan line.

Our forces are entangled across the western frontier. I propose A MAR hold and no Austrian move into PIE or your other centers this spring, if A PIE and A MUN stay out of MAR, TYR, and Austrian centers. What are your orders for A PIE, A MUN, and A VEN?

I want to prevent the Rumanian dispute becoming a wider war. What are F RUM, A SEV, and A UKR doing this spring? Keep A GAL and A SER clear of your centers, and please keep your units out of GAL, SER, and Austrian centers.

Can we agree to keep the Balkans quiet this spring? I will not move A SER or F GRE against your centers; please keep F BLA and A CON clear of SER, GRE, and BUL. Are you willing to coordinate pressure on F RUM, and what are your orders for F BLA and A CON?

England to France, Spring 1912: Your Belgium promise was broken again. A Bel still sits in Belgium. Show deeds this spring: A Bel leaves for Holland or Ruhr, A Pic does not enter Picardy, and F Bre stays out of the Channel. Then my North Sea fleets stay north. Otherwise F Nth and F Nor go west.

Your A MAR is a direct threat to my A GAS and A PIE. What are A MAR and A SER doing this spring? I can keep my armies out of your centers if you keep A MAR from advancing into GAS or PIE and avoid attacks on my units.

I want to avoid a western war while facing pressure from Austria. What are F NTH, F NOR, and A SWE doing this spring? I will keep my fleets away from the Channel and your centers if your fleets stay clear of Brest and Picardy.

Austria's A MAR threatens my southern flank. Are you willing to coordinate against Austria this spring? I can move against Austrian positions from MUN and VEN; please tell me whether A BER and your fleets will stay clear of my centers.

Germany to Austria, Spring 1912: My A Ber and F Kie stay in place this spring and will not enter Bohemia or Silesia. Your units are at Mun and Bud, so I assume you're focused on Russia and Italy. Please keep your forces out of Berlin, Kiel and Holland, and tell me your spring moves.

Russia to Austria, Spring 1912: A Rumania is still an Austrian army on Russian-claimed soil, and our history of broken truces makes me wary. Withdraw A Rum to Hungary or Bohemia this spring and I will keep A Sev and F Rum-area forces off Galicia and Serbia. Tell me your concrete plan for A Rum and A Ser before I move.

Austria's A SER and F GRE leave the Balkans tightly held, while BUL appears open. I propose A CON–BUL with F BLA supporting. Will F RUM stay clear or support the move, and what are A SEV and F RUM doing this spring? I want coordination against Austrian expansion, not a contest with you.

The Balkan freeze has left Turkey with no room to grow. BUL appears open, and I intend to seek a position there this spring. What are A SER and F GRE doing? I would prefer a clear boundary and no attack on Turkish centers, but cannot accept an indefinite freeze.

Your A VEN and F ADR are well placed to pressure Austria. I am considering a move from A CON toward BUL; would you press Austrian positions from VEN or elsewhere this spring? I will keep Turkish units away from your Italian centers, and would welcome coordination that makes Austria divide its forces.

A RUM will remain in place this spring; I cannot abandon it while Turkish forces press the Balkans. A SER will not move against you, and A GAL will stay out of your centers. Keep A SEV and F RUM-area forces out of Galicia, Serbia, and Austrian centers, and we can contain the dispute.

My spring focus is not Berlin, Kiel, or Holland; Austrian units will stay clear of your centers. I am handling the eastern and western fronts. Please keep your forces out of Austrian territory, and let me know if France approaches Munich.

A MAR will hold this spring; I will not advance it into GAS or PIE or attack your units. A SER is not moving against French interests. In return, keep A PIE and A MUN out of MAR, TYR, and Austrian centers, as proposed.

I cannot promise an indefinite freeze, but A SER and F GRE will not attack Turkish centers this spring. I cannot leave BUL open while F BLA and A CON may move there; keep them clear of SER, GRE, and BUL, and we can discuss coordinated pressure on F RUM.

England to France, Spring 1912: Words have failed repeatedly. A Bel is still in Belgium and A Pic is still in Picardy. I will hold my fleets on the North Sea line for now, but I see no proof you will leave Belgium. Move A Bel out this spring and keep F Bre out of the Channel, and we can talk. Otherwise F Nth and F Nor go west.

I will move A BEL to BUR this spring and keep A PIC in place. There is no French F BRE; my fleets are F MAO and F ADR, and neither will enter the Channel or an English center. Please keep F NTH and F NOR north and clear of Brest and Picardy.

A PIE will hold, A MUN will hold, and A VEN will support A PIE holding. I will not move into MAR, TYR, or an Austrian center this spring. Please keep A MAR from advancing into PIE or GAS, as proposed, and keep A SER clear of my units.

Yes—please press from A CON toward BUL. I will use A VEN to support A PIE holding against A MAR, while A MUN holds. F ADR will stay out of your Italian centers. If Austria attacks, we can coordinate further in the fall.

Germany to France: I will keep A Ber and F Kie and F Hol at home this spring and will not enter Belgium, Picardy or your other centers. But I have seen French armies press Munich and Ruhr before, so do not expect my support against Austria. Keep A Mun and A Ven away from Tyrolia and Piedmont-to-Berlin routes, and we stay at peace.

Russia to Austria: A Rumania remains an Austrian army on Russian-claimed soil, and I will not accept that. Withdraw A Rum to Hungary or Bohemia this spring and I will keep A Sev and F Rum off Galicia and Serbia. Keep A Gal and A Ser out of Warsaw and Ukraine. Otherwise my forces will defend Sevastopol and Rumania.

Russia to Turkey: I will not support A Con-Bul and F Rum will not move to Bulgaria. Your A Con-Bul is a matter for you and Austria. Keep F Bla out of Sevastopol and Rumania, and keep Turkish units away from my centers. A Russo-Turkish line can hold if you respect it.

I’m willing to keep the Balkans quiet only with a workable boundary. I intend A CON–BUL this spring and will keep F BLA clear of SER and GRE; I cannot promise to leave BUL untouched. Please keep A SER and F GRE off Turkish centers. I’m open to coordinating pressure on A RUM, but need your specific proposal.

For this fall, I propose a limited western frontier: A MAR and A TYR will not move against your units or centers. Please keep A PIE, A MUN, A RUH, and A BUR out of Austrian centers and avoid advancing toward VIE or TYR. Can we hold that boundary?

Can we settle a clear Balkan boundary this fall? I propose A SER–BUL with F GRE supporting; please keep A CON and F BLA out of BUL, SER, and GRE. In return, I will not order A SER or F GRE against your centers. Are you willing to leave BUL to me?

Can we avoid widening the eastern dispute this fall? I will keep A SER and A TYR clear of Russian centers; please keep F RUM and A SEV out of Serbia, Galicia, and Austrian centers. Let me know whether you intend to press into the Balkans or can hold the line.

England to France, Fall 1912: Your Belgium and Picardy promises have failed again, and A Bel, A Pic and F Wes now sit near our coasts. Show deeds this fall: A Bel out of Belgium, no French unit into Picardy, Brest or any English center. Then F Nth and F Nor stay north. Otherwise my fleets go west.

Our forces remain close on the western frontier. I will keep A MUN, A PIE, and A VEN out of Austrian centers this fall if A MAR and A TYR stay out of my centers and do not attack my units. What are A MAR and A SER doing?

A BEL is no longer in Belgium, and I have no fleet in the Channel. I will keep my units out of English centers and keep F WES and F ADR away from the Channel coast. Please keep F NTH and F NOR north; what are they doing this fall?

Austria remains vulnerable from the south and west. Are you moving A CON or other units against Austrian positions this fall? I can pressure Austria from A VEN or A MUN, but need to know your plan before committing.

Germany to England, Fall 1912: F Kie and F Hol stay put this fall and I will not enter Belgium or Denmark. Please keep F Nth and F Nor away from Holland and Kiel. I'm willing to discuss a northern line once we see where France and Austria push, so tell me your fall moves.

Germany to France, Fall 1912: A Ber, F Kie and F Hol stay home and I won't move into Belgium, Picardy or your centers. Keep A Bur, A Ruh and A Mun away from Berlin, Kiel and Holland. Tell me whether your western armies will stay out of German territory this fall.

Germany to Russia, Fall 1912: I have no intention of attacking you and keep my units in Germany. Austria is the power pressing Germany and your southern flank. Will your armies in Warsaw and Ukraine stay out of my centers? I am open to a quiet understanding while we both watch Austria.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1912: F Bla must stay out of Sevastopol and Rumania, and A Arm must not enter Sevastopol or Rumania. I will keep F Rum and A Sev out of Bulgaria and Constantinople. Confirm in writing, and tell me whether A Con and A Arm will stay clear of Armenia and Rumania this fall.

Russia to Austria, Fall 1912: Your A Rum has left Rumania, which I welcome. I will keep A Sev and F Rum off Galicia and Serbia if A Gal, A Bud, and A Ser stay out of Warsaw, Ukraine, and Rumania. Tell me your concrete plan for A Bud and A Ser this fall.

BUL remains the point of friction after our spring bounce. What are A SER and F GRE doing this fall? I intend to try A CON–BUL again with F BLA support; please say whether you will contest it, and whether you will keep your units off Turkish centers.

I will keep F BLA clear of RUM and SEV and my units away from Russian centers. What are F RUM and A SEV doing this fall? I may renew A CON–BUL with F BLA support; will you stay clear of BUL so we avoid another contest?

Austria still holds a strong position around the Balkans. I’m considering renewing A CON–BUL with F BLA support. Can you pressure Austria this fall from VEN or elsewhere, and what are A VEN and F ADR doing? I’ll keep Turkish units away from your centers.

A BUD and A SER will stay clear of Warsaw, Ukraine, and Rumania this fall. I intend to keep the eastern line quiet; please keep F RUM and A SEV out of Serbia, Galicia, and Austrian centers. A SER's exact order will depend on whether Turkey again contests Bulgaria.

I will contest your A CON–BUL attempt: A SER will move to BUL, with F GRE supporting. Keep F BLA and A CON out of SER and GRE, and do not attack Austrian centers; I will keep A SER and F GRE off Turkish centers.

A MAR and A TYR will stay out of French centers and will not attack your units this fall. Please keep A PIE, A MUN, A RUH, and A BUR out of Austrian centers and avoid advancing toward VIE or TYR; we can maintain the boundary.

England to Germany, Fall 1912: My F Nth and F Nor will not enter Holland, Kiel or Denmark this fall. I am moving them away from your home centers. Hold Kiel and Berlin and we stay at peace. If you move on Denmark or Sweden, I will know and respond. Let us keep the northern line calm while France and Austria fight.

England to France, Fall 1912: Your units still sit on our coast: A Pic and A Bel are too close to London and Liverpool. Words are cheap. Pull A Pic out of Picardy and A Bel out of Belgium, and keep F Wes off the Channel. Then F Nth and F Nor stay north. If Picardy or Brest see French units heading toward English centers, my fleets go west.

A Bel is now in Ruh, not Belgium; I have no F Bre. I’ll keep my units out of English centers and F Wes and F Adr away from the Channel coast. Please keep F Nth and F Nor north and clear of Brest and Picardy.
I’ll keep A Bur, A Ruh, and A Mun out of German territory this fall. I’m not seeking a western war while Austria threatens my flank; please keep your units at home as you propose.

Please renew A Con–Bul with F Bla support. I can pressure Austria from A Ven, but need your commitment against Bul and clarity on whether Austria is defending its Balkan line. F Adr will stay out of Turkish centers.

I can keep A Pie, A Mun, A Ruh, and A Bur out of Austrian centers and avoid advancing toward Vie or Tyr this fall, provided A Mar and A Tyr do not attack my units or centers. Please confirm your units will hold that boundary.

Russia to Germany: Thanks. My armies in Warsaw and Ukraine are defensive and will stay out of your centers Berlin, Holland and Kiel. I have no designs on Prussia this fall. Austria is the threat to both of us; if you keep Silesia and Bohemia watched, we can keep our understanding.

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1912: F Rum and A Sev will not move into Bulgaria or Constantinople, and I will not support any attack on Bulgaria. F Bla must stay out of Sevastopol and Rumania, and A Arm must not enter Rumania or Sevastopol. Respect that and we have a line. Break it and I defend Sevastopol.

Russia to Austria: Your A Rum has left, and I appreciate it. I keep A Sev and F Rum off Galicia and Serbia as long as A Gal, A Bud and A Ser stay out of Warsaw, Ukraine and Rumania. Bud and Ser should hold or move toward Trieste or Vienna, not east. Confirm that and we keep the peace.

Confirmed: F BLA will stay clear of RUM and SEV, and A ARM will stay clear of both RUM and SEV. I will keep Turkish units away from Russian centers. I may renew A CON–BUL with F BLA support; please keep F RUM and A SEV clear of BUL and CON.

I intend to renew A CON–BUL with F BLA support, and A ARM will stay out of Austrian centers. Austria proposes A SER–BUL supported by F GRE, so a direct contest may bounce. Can you pressure Austria from VEN or MUN—particularly toward TRI, TYR, or BOH—and tell me your specific move?

I cannot agree to leave BUL to you; it is the only practical opening for Turkey. I intend A CON–BUL with F BLA support, and will keep A ARM and F BLA clear of SER and GRE. Please keep A SER and F GRE off Turkish centers; we can avoid a wider Balkan war even if BUL remains disputed.
