Russia to France, Spring 1920: Your A Boh and A Vie sit near my Warsaw and Ukraine. I will keep A War and A Ukr out of Boh and Vie while no French unit enters Warsaw, Rumania or Sevastopol. Tell me your exact Spring orders for A Bud, A Ser, A Ruh and A Gas so I can verify them before I move.

France is the dominant threat, and I can attack A SER from TRI with BUL support this spring. Can you pressure GAL or another French position from your side? I will stay out of RUM and SEV; please give me your concrete orders so we can avoid conflict.

France holds most of central Europe and the south, while your fleets are well placed in the north. Will you pressure France this spring, and what target can you take? I can move against its Balkan positions; a coordinated attack is our best chance to contain it.

Your forces still threaten my frontier, especially A SER and A VIE. I intend to contest your Balkan positions this spring. Are you willing to pull back from SER and keep F ADR clear of Turkish territory, or should I expect you to defend them?

England to Germany, Spring 1920: F Nth will hold in the North Sea this spring and F Den will hold in place. I will not move into Hol or Kie. If French units move on Hol, Den, or Bel, we can talk about coordinating. I'm also watching Russia in the Baltic, so keep your eastern border secure.

England to Turkey, Spring 1920: I am not attacking France from the west this spring. My fleets stay in the North Sea and Baltic, and I am focusing on Russia's northern and Baltic positions. Run your Balkan operations as you see fit. I'll tell you if French units head toward Spain or Portugal.

England to France, Spring 1920: Noted. I will keep F Nth and F Den north and out of the Channel this spring. I make no promises about German centers, and I will watch Bel and Pic closely. Any French move into Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den, or the Channel ends our understanding at once.

A BUD, A SER, A RUH, and A GAS are not French units on the current board. My exact orders for A SIL and A VIE are not for your territory; I will not enter WAR, RUM, or SEV this spring. Please keep A WAR and A MOS away from SIL and GAL, and oppose Turkish moves into SER or BUL.

I cannot promise that A RUH, A SIL, or A MUN will stay out of HOL, KIE, and DEN; I intend to secure French interests in Germany. I will not move into French territory, and I am not making peace while you retain forces at HOL and KIE. A BER is already French.

I will defend A SER and A VIE if you contest them. F ADR will stay clear of Turkish territory, and I will not move A SER into BUL. Keep A TRI and A BUL out of SER and VIE, and keep your fleets out of ADR and ROM; otherwise expect resistance.

Russia to England: Thanks for the offer. Russia wants Sweden and the Baltic kept calm, but I will not commit to attacking France now. Keep F Stp and A Swe out of Moscow and Warsaw, and I will do the same for your Sweden and Norway. Let us talk again once French moves are clearer.

Russia to Germany: I hear your call against France, but I will not move A War toward Silesia or Berlin this spring. Keep F Hol and F Kie out of Livonia and Warsaw, and I will keep my armies on my own frontier. Show me a concrete French target first and we can reassess.

Russia to Turkey: Once again I am not committing A War or A Ukr against France this spring. Hold your A Tri and A Bul out of Rumania and Sevastopol and I will keep F Rum and A Sev in place. Attack Serbia if you must, but show me Greek or Serbian results before I judge further cooperation.

Russia to France: Agreed in principle. I will keep A War and A Mos out of Silesia and Galicia while no French unit enters Warsaw, Rumania or Sevastopol. I will not oppose Turkish moves into Serbia or Bulgaria, but I want your Spring orders for A Bud, A Ser, A Ruh and A Gas before I move anything.

I cannot leave A SER uncontested while your armies remain on my frontier. I will keep A TRI and A BUL out of VIE, and my fleets out of ADR and ROM, but I intend to attack SER from TRI with support from BUL. Keep F ADR out of TRI and your units out of Turkish centers; we can avoid expanding the conflict beyond SER.

England to France, Fall 1920: Your units in Germany and Russia's reach are far from my islands. Confirm plainly that A Bud, A Gal, A Pru and A Ruh will not enter Den, Nor, Swe or the Channel, and tell me whether F Nap or A Naf is moving toward Spain or Portugal. I will keep F Nth and F Den north.

England to Germany, Fall 1920: Kiel and Holland are your business, not mine. I will not move F Nth or F Den into Hol or Kie. Tell me plainly what A Ruh and A Mun intend, since France's armies are near your border. If you move on Bel or Pic, I want to hear it first.

England to Russia, Fall 1920: Keep A Mos and A War out of Swe and Nor, and I will keep F Stp and A Swe clear of Mos and War. Are you planning to take Ukr or Gal from France or Austria? Tell me your fall orders so we avoid collision.

Your forces at SER and TRI threaten my Balkan centers, while mine can press yours. I propose a clear line this fall: keep A BUL and A TRI out of BUD and SER, and I will keep A SER and A TRI out of BUL and CON. Will you agree, or are you moving against my centers?

I intend to settle the Turkish threat and do not plan to enter WAR, RUM, or SEV this fall. Will you keep A MOS and A WAR away from my eastern positions, and can you contest Turkey's A BUL or A SEV rather than support a move against me?

With your remaining centers exposed, I propose you keep F HEL and F HOL out of KIE and my centers this fall; I will avoid attacking your units directly if you do. What are your orders for those fleets? I cannot offer a lasting guarantee while Germany remains a threat to my position.

Germany to France, Fall 1920: Germany has lost BER and MUN in practice; I have only HOL and KIE. Your A BUR, A RUH and A PIC sit on my border. Name each French unit's exact fall move in writing now. If any French unit enters HOL, KIE or DEN, I will counterattack in Ruhr and Burgundy at once.

Russia to France, Fall 1920: Your board units do not match what you described, so I need exact orders. Any French move into Warsaw, Rumania or Sevastopol ends our understanding. I will hold A War, A Ukr and F Rum while I see your Fall moves against Germany and Turkey.

Russia to Germany: Your F Hol and F Kie stay out of Livonia and Warsaw, and I hold A War. If you retake Berlin or Munich from France, I am open to talks on Silesia later. Tell me your Fall orders first.

Russia to Turkey: I hold F Rum and A Sev this fall and will not enter Bulgaria or Constantinople. Keep A Bul and A Ser off Rumania. Show me results against Serbia or Greece, and I will judge further cooperation next season.

France still dominates the center and has A GAL beside your frontier. Can you move A UKR to GAL or otherwise pressure GAL this fall? I can coordinate from SER/BUL, but need to know whether you plan to contest SEV or RUM.

France remains the main threat, with forces across the Balkans and central Europe. Are you willing to pressure it from the west this fall? Please name a concrete target and intended unit; I can keep my eastern moves coordinated with that pressure.

Please confirm your fall intentions for A TRI, A BUD, and F ADR. I want to avoid your centers, but cannot leave French forces pressing my Balkan position unchecked. If you keep F ADR out of Turkish territory and avoid advancing into BUL or CON, we can limit the conflict.

England to Turkey, Fall 1920: I will not pressure France from the west this fall. My fleets stay in the North Sea and Baltic, and I have no unit that can reach Brest, Spain or Portugal in time. Run your Balkan and Eastern moves as you see fit. I will watch Russia's northern positions and tell you if France sends fleets toward the Channel or Iberia.

My actual units include A RUH, A KIE, and A BUR. I intend to move A RUH to HOL, with A KIE supporting, and will not promise to leave your last centers untouched. I have no reason to move against your fleets in HEL.

I will not move into WAR, RUM, or SEV this fall. Please keep A MOS and A WAR away from my eastern positions, and use A UKR or A SEV to contest Turkey rather than threaten my units. I am focusing on the Turkish and German fronts.
Those units are not on my board: I have A BUD, A PRU, and A RUH, but no A GAL. I will keep my forces out of DEN, NOR, SWE, and the Channel. F NAP and A NAF are not moving toward your centers.

I will keep F ADR out of Turkish territory and will not move A TRI or A BUD into BUL or CON. Your A SER and A TRI remain a threat to my Balkan centers, so I will defend them; do not move A BUL or A TRI into BUD or SER.

Germany to France: I will not promise peace while your A BUR, A RUH and A PIC press my borders. My fall orders for F HEL and F HOL are not yet set; I will decide after you name each French unit's exact fall move in writing. Any French entry into HOL, KIE or DEN means immediate war.

Germany to Russia: Thank you for holding A WAR. My F HOL and F KIE will not enter Livonia or Warsaw. I am focused on France now. If you keep your armies on your own frontier, I am willing to discuss Silesia once Berlin and Munich are back in my hands. Share your fall orders.

Germany to England: I hear you on Kiel and Holland. I will not move on Belgium or Picardy this fall without telling you first. Please keep F Nth and F Den out of Hol and Kie, as I am doing. A Ruh and A Mun are still under review; France has not named its exact moves, and I will report what I learn.

Russia to England: Our fall plans remain defensive. A Mos and A War will not enter Swe or Nor, and I expect F Stp and A Swe to stay clear of Mos and War as well. I hold my positions this fall and have no plans against Ukr or Gal yet. Let us keep the Baltic calm and talk again next season.

Russia to France: Your board units still do not match what you described, so I cannot take your word alone. Any French move into Warsaw, Rumania or Sevastopol ends our understanding at once. I hold A War, A Ukr and F Rum this fall. Show me your exact Fall moves against Germany and Turkey, and I will judge from there.

Russia to Turkey: I hold F Rum and A Sev this fall and will not enter Bulgaria or Constantinople. I am not moving A Ukr to Gal this fall; my forces stay on my frontier. Keep A Bul and A Ser out of Rumania and Sevastopol. Show me concrete results against Serbia or Greece first.

I can show a result against France: A SER will attack TRI with support from A BUL. I will keep A BUL and A SER off RUM, and won’t contest SEV. Please move A UKR to GAL to pressure France’s eastern flank; I’ll let you know how the attack resolves.

I can’t agree to leave your Balkan position uncontested. A SER will attack TRI with support from A BUL. I’ll keep A BUL out of BUD and SER, and keep my units out of BUL and CON; please keep A TRI out of BUL and CON as you proposed.

England to France, Spring 1921: Your board is huge, with 15 centers and many armies near my shores. Confirm plainly that your fleets will not enter Nth, Nor, Den, or the Channel this spring. In return I will keep my fleets out of Bel, Pic and Bre. If you want peace, say what you will do with A Bel and A Bre.

I will keep my forces out of your centers and the Channel this spring. Please keep your fleets out of BEL and the Channel, and tell me whether you intend to press Germany or move against my northern centers.
Your F HOL is isolated. I intend to move A RUH to HOL; do you plan to defend it or will you withdraw? I will not move against KIE this spring if you keep F HOL from interfering with my forces.
Your A BUL and A SER threaten my A TRI and Balkan position. I propose you keep A BUL out of SER and A SER out of TRI this spring; I will keep A TRI out of BUL and CON. What are your intentions?

Germany to France, Spring 1921: Your A RUH and A KIE are now on my last centers. Name each French unit's exact spring move in writing now. Any French unit moving into HOL, KIE or DEN means immediate war, and I will hit your Ruhr and Burgundy armies at once.

Russia to Turkey: I hold A Mos and A Rum this spring. Your F Bla is the threat to Rumania, so keep it out of Rum and Sev and I will not contest Bul or Con. Share your Spring orders for A Ser and A Bul, and whether you will strike French Tri or Bud.

Russia to France: I hold A Mos and A Rum and will not move toward Gal or Ukr this spring. Your understanding stands only while no French unit enters Warsaw, Rumania or Sevastopol. Tell me your exact Spring moves against Germany and Turkey so I can judge our frontier.

France remains the dominant threat, and its A WAR/A SIL are exposed to pressure. This spring I can attack A TRI from SER with BUL support. Can you move A RUM to GAL to pressure its flank? I will keep my units out of RUM and SEV; please confirm your orders.

France still controls the center and south. Are you willing to pressure it this spring? Please name a concrete target and unit. My forces can contest its Balkan position, but western pressure would make that more effective.

Your A TRI remains beside my Balkan centers. I propose limiting the conflict: keep A TRI out of SER and F ADR out of Turkish territory, and I will keep my armies out of VIE and BUD. Are you willing to agree, or should I expect you to defend TRI?

England to France, Spring 1921: I will not move F Nth, F Nor or F Den into Nth, Nor, Den or the Channel this spring, and my fleets stay out of Bel, Pic and Bre. A Bel and A Bre are your business as long as they stay on your side of the Channel. Keep your word on Lon, Edi and Lvp, and we remain at peace.

England to Turkey, Spring 1921: I cannot pressure France from the west this spring. My fleets are in the North Sea and Baltic, and none can reach Brest, Spain or Portugal in time. Run your Balkan campaign as you see fit. I will keep watching Russia's northern positions and will tell you if French fleets head for the Channel or Iberia.
A RUH will move to HOL, supported by A KIE. I will not move against DEN or KIE this spring. F HOL can withdraw or defend as you choose; I’m not offering to leave your last center untouched.
My fleets will stay out of the Nth, Nor, Den and Channel this spring. A Bel and A Bre will stay clear of Pic and the Channel. Please keep your fleets out of Bel, Pic and Bre as proposed.

Against Germany, A RUH moves to HOL with support from A KIE. I will not enter WAR, RUM or SEV, and have no plans to move into Gal or Ukr. I’ll keep A TRI out of SER and focus on defending my Balkan position.

Agreed: A TRI will stay out of SER, and F ADR will stay out of Turkish territory this spring. I expect A BUL to stay out of SER and A SER to stay out of TRI, as proposed; keep your armies out of VIE and BUD.

Germany to France, Spring 1921: Your A RUH to HOL is an attack on my last fleet and my last centers, and I will treat it as war. F HOL will hold and defend. Keep A KIE out of my territory too. If you move A RUH to HOL, I will counter with every unit I have against your Ruhr and Burgundy armies. Withdraw A RUH now and state it in writing.

Russia to Turkey: I am not moving A Rum to Gal this spring; my A Mos and A Rum hold their positions. Your F Bla must stay out of Rum and Sev, and I will judge your cooperation by results against Tri or Bud. If your A Ser attacks Tri with Bul support, I will note it. Confirm your A Bul and A Ser orders in writing.

A SER will attack TRI, supported by A BUL. I will keep my forces out of RUM and SEV. Please move A RUM to GAL as requested; that would put useful pressure on France’s flank. I cannot promise to keep A SER out of TRI.

I cannot agree to keep A SER out of TRI: it will attack TRI with support from A BUL. I will keep A BUL out of SER and my armies out of VIE and BUD; my fleets will stay out of ADR and ROM. You should expect to defend TRI.

England to France, Fall 1921: Your fleets have been kept out of my waters, and I have kept mine out of Bel, Pic and Bre. Confirm that A Bel and A Bre stay on your side of the Channel this fall and that no French unit enters Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den or the Channel. I hold F Nth and F Den north; I will not enter Hol or Kie.

I intend to keep my forces out of the Channel, NTH, NOR, and your centers this fall. Please keep your fleets clear of BEL, PIC, and BRE. With Germany nearly finished, will you stay out of my northern centers while I secure the German position?
I intend to move A HOL to HEL, with A KIE supporting. Your F HEL is isolated; I am not proposing a truce that leaves it in place. Do you intend to contest HEL or withdraw?

I expect A SER and A BUL to attack TRI again. A BUD will support A TRI holding, and F ADR will stay out of your territory. I will keep A TRI out of BUL and CON; will you keep A BUL out of BUD and avoid further attacks on TRI?

Germany to Russia, Fall 1921: Germany is down to HOL and HEL, and France holds BER, MUN and KIE-side armies. I need a real counter-move. Will your A UKR or A MOS move toward WAR or LVN to pressure France's eastern holdings? Tell me your exact fall orders so we can coordinate on Silesia and Berlin.

Russia to Turkey: Your Spring Tri attack is noted. Results matter now. Your F Tys and F Rom threaten nothing of mine, but F Bla near Rum or Sev would end our understanding. Confirm whether A Ser actually moves to Tri this Fall, and whether A Bul will support it. I will keep A Mos and A Rum off Gal only while you stay out of my southern coast.

France remains the main threat, but I need room to secure centers. I will keep my forces out of RUM and SEV this fall. Can you avoid BUL and CON and use A UKR to pressure French-held WAR or LVN? I can press France from the south.

France controls most of the board and is vulnerable in the south. Can you make a concrete move against a French center this fall—such as F STP/NORTH toward Norway or a fleet move against the western coast—and tell me which unit? I will attack France from the south.

Your army at TRI and fleet at TUS leave my forces exposed to pressure. I intend to contest French positions this fall, but would prefer a limited settlement: keep A TRI and F TUS away from my centers, and I will avoid BUD and VIE. Are you willing?

England to Turkey, Fall 1921: I cannot make a concrete move against France this fall. My fleets stay in the North Sea and Baltic, and none can reach Brest or the western coast in time. F STP/NORTH is needed to hold my northern centers. Keep pressing France in the Balkans and Italy; I will watch the Channel and report any French fleet heading west.

England to France, Fall 1921: I confirm my fleets will not enter Bel, Pic or Bre, and I will not move F Nth or F Den into Hol, Kie or the Channel. In return, A Bel and A Bre must stay on your side of the Channel, and no French unit may enter Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den or the Channel. I cannot promise anything about German centers. Keep your word and we remain at peace.

A Bel and A Bre will stay on my side of the Channel, and no French unit will enter Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den, or the Channel this fall. Please keep F Nth and F Den north out of Bel, Pic, and Bre. I am securing the German position; do not move against my northern centers.

I cannot promise to leave A TRI away from your centers while your forces threaten it. F TUS will stay clear of your centers this fall, and F ADR will stay out of Turkish territory. Keep A BUL out of BUD and avoid further attacks on TRI; I will defend TRI and BUD.

Germany to France: Your A HOL to HEL with A KIE support is a direct attack on my fleet and I will treat it as war. F HEL will hold and defend. Pull A KIE and A HOL back out of my space now, in writing, or every German unit I have will strike your Ruhr and Burgundy armies.

Russia to Germany: I understand your position. My A Ukr and A Mos are still weighing options, and I have not yet fixed my Fall orders. Any German move that threatens Warsaw or Livonia from the west would be welcome, but I will not commit to a Silesia deal until I see Berlin or Munich change hands. Show me your exact orders first.

A SER will attack TRI this Fall with support from A BUL. I will keep my forces out of RUM and SEV, including F RUM. Please use A UKR to pressure French-held WAR or LVN; I will continue pressing France from the south.

I will keep A BUL out of BUD, but A SER will attack TRI with support from A BUL. I cannot agree to leave TRI unchallenged while your army there threatens my Balkan position. I will keep my forces out of VIE and BUD, and F ADR out of my territory.

England to France, Spring 1922: Your fleets have kept out of my waters, and I have kept mine off Bel, Pic and Bre. I will not move F Nth or F Den toward Hol, Kie or the Channel. Confirm that A Bel, A Hol and F Bre stay on your side, and that no French unit enters Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den or the Channel this spring. I see your massing on the German border; tell me plainly your intentions there.

England to Turkey, Spring 1922: I still cannot strike France from the west this spring, as my fleets are needed in the North Sea and Baltic to hold Nor, Den and Stp. Keep pressuring France in the Balkans and Italy. If French fleets move toward the Channel or Iberia I will tell you at once.

I’m concentrating east this spring and will keep my forces out of your centers and the Channel. Please keep your fleets clear of BEL, PIC, and BRE and avoid moving against my northern centers; can we maintain the existing nonaggression while I deal with Turkey?

I expect the contest over TRI to continue. I will press into SER unless you are willing to withdraw A SER and keep A BUL out of my Balkan centers. If you do, I’m prepared to discuss a limited settlement; otherwise, tell me where you intend to commit your forces.

France is close to an 18-center win, so I cannot leave your position uncontested. I intend to pressure TRI from SER and BUL this spring. Keep A TRI from attacking my centers and F ADR out of my territory; I will avoid BUD and VIE. Can you agree to that limited line?

France controls 16 centers and is two from victory. Can you open pressure on a French center this spring—specifically, what will F DEN, F LVP, or your armies target? I will press France from TRI and Italy; coordinated pressure is our best chance to stop its win.

England to Turkey, Spring 1922: My fleets must hold Nor, Den and Stp this spring, so F Den and F Lvp will not head for the Channel or Bel. Keep your pressure on France from TRI, Bud and Italy, and tell me which French center you will hit first so we can coordinate later.

England to France, Spring 1922: Agreed. I will keep F Nth and F Den out of Bel, Pic, Bre, Hol and Kie this spring, and my fleets will stay out of the Channel. Please keep A Bel, A Hol and F Bre on your side, and no French unit enters Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den or the Channel. We remain at peace.

Confirmed: A BEL, A HOL, and F BRE stay on my side; no French unit enters your centers or the Channel this spring. My northern concentration is to secure the German position and guard against surprises, not to threaten you. Keep F NTH and F DEN clear of HOL, KIE, BEL, PIC, and BRE, and we can maintain the line.

I cannot agree to leave TRI unchallenged while A SER and A BUL threaten it. F ADR will stay out of your territory, and I will avoid BUD and VIE if you withdraw A SER from the TRI front and keep A BUL out of my Balkan centers. Otherwise I will defend TRI and press where I can.

France has 17 centers and is one from victory. Please put F DEN toward KIE this spring to threaten a French center; F LVP can move to IRI, and A LON toward WAL. I’ll attack from SER and Italy. Even a direct threat may force France to divert units.

I cannot agree to withdraw A SER while you retain A TRI and threaten SER; France is one center from victory, so I must contest your position. A BUL will support the defense of SER. Keep A TRI out of SER and F ADR out of my territory, and I will continue avoiding BUD and VIE.

England to Turkey, Fall 1922: France is near 18 centers, so we must stop it now. I will move F Den to Hel and F Lvp toward Iri, threatening Bel and Bre next turn, and A Lon toward Wal. Please hit Tri and Bud with A Ser and A Bul, and tell me which French center you will take first.

England to France, Fall 1922: Your massing on the German border and your growing centre count worry me. I keep my word on Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor and Den for now, but I will not let France reach 18 unopposed. Tell me plainly whether your A Bel, A Hol and F Bre will stay on your side this autumn.

I will keep A BEL, A HOL and F BRE out of your centers and the Channel this fall. Please keep F DEN and F STP/NORTH clear of my centers and northern units while I settle the Balkan front. Can we maintain our nonaggression line?

Your A SER and A BUL keep TRI under pressure, so I cannot accept a quiet line while they remain there. I intend to press the front this fall. If you will withdraw A SER from TRI and keep A BUL out of my Balkan centers, we can discuss a ceasefire; otherwise I will continue the contest.

France still dominates the board. This fall, please move F DEN to KIE to threaten a French center; A SWE can support it from BER only if France attacks, so at least make the direct move. I’ll press France from the south. Can you commit to that?

Your armies at SER-facing TRI and the southern fleets make a settlement difficult, but I want to prevent either of us wasting forces. Keep A TRI out of SER and F ADR out of Turkish centers; I will avoid BUD and VIE. I will continue contesting your positions elsewhere.

England to Turkey: My fleets are committed to the north this fall, so F Den will not go to Kie. I plan to bring F Lvp toward Iri and A Lon toward Wal, and I will watch France's western coast. Keep pressing Tri and Bud. Please take Tri or Bud first; I will report any French move into the Channel or Iberia immediately.

A BEL and A HOL will stay on my side, and F MAO will not enter the Channel or your centers this autumn. I will keep clear of Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor and Den. Please keep F DEN and F STP/NORTH clear of my centers and northern positions while I finish the Balkan contest.

A TRI will not move to SER this autumn, and F ADR will stay out of Turkish centers. I cannot agree to a broader ceasefire while A SER and A BUL remain positioned against TRI; I will continue defending my Balkan centers. Keep A BUL out of BUD and VIE, as proposed.

I’ll make Tri the priority from the south; A SER will be committed against it, with support from A BUL if the position allows. Please follow through with F LVP to IRI and A LON toward WAL, and keep France under pressure in the west. Let me know if you see a French move that changes the balance.

I will not withdraw A SER while France holds TRI and your forces can threaten my Balkan position. I am prepared to avoid BUD and VIE, provided F ADR stays out of Turkish centers and A TRI does not attack SER. I intend to keep pressing TRI; we can revisit a ceasefire if the front changes.

England to France, Spring 1923: Your fleets have stayed off my centers, and I will keep F Nth and F Den out of Bel, Hol, Kie, Bre and Pic this spring. Confirm A Bel, A Hol and A Kie stay clear of Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den, Swe and Stp. Your Ruhr and Lvn massing is my concern; tell me plainly if Kie or Den is your target this year.

England to Turkey, Spring 1923: France holds 16 centers and is close to victory. I will keep F Den and F Lvp in the north and not commit them to the Channel yet, but I want a real move from you. Tell me which French center your A Tri, A Ser and A Bud will take this spring, and I will weigh a fleet move against France accordingly.

I will keep A BEL, A HOL and F MAO clear of your centers and the Channel this spring. My armies are focused east; please keep F HEL, F STP/NORTH and your other units clear of my centers. Can we maintain the nonaggression line through this turn?

Your A TRI is in my center, while my forces hold the Balkan front. What are your intentions for A TRI and A SER this spring? I can discuss a ceasefire if you withdraw from TRI and keep your forces out of BUD and VIE; otherwise I will continue defending my position.

France still has a path to 18, so we need simultaneous pressure. Can you move F HEL to KIE and A SWE to BER this spring to threaten French centers? I’ll hold A TRI and use my southern units to press France; please tell me which French center you can actually target.

France remains the chief threat to everyone. I intend to keep A TRI in place and will not attack SER or your other Balkan centers this spring. Will you keep A TRI out of SER and your fleets out of Turkish centers, and avoid attacking my position while we both contain the northern threat?

England to France, Spring 1923: I will keep F Nth, F Den and F Hel out of Bel, Hol, Kie, Bre and Pic this spring, and my fleets stay out of the Channel. In return, A Bel, A Hol and A Kie must stay clear of Lon, Edi, Lvp, Nor, Den, Swe and Stp, and no French fleet enters the Channel or Iberia toward my coast. Your Ruhr and Lvn massing worries me. Kie is the key; if you move on it, I will know. Tell me plainly your target.

England to Turkey, Spring 1923: I will not move F Hel to Kie or A Swe to Ber while France keeps its armies on my flank. My fleets stay north to hold Nor, Den and Stp. Your Tri, Ser and Bud must actually strike a French center this spring, such as Bud or Rum, before I commit anything. Show me a real attack first and I will weigh a western move.

A BEL, A HOL and A KIE will stay clear of your centers this spring; I have no plan to move on DEN this year. My immediate effort is east and south, not against England. Please keep F HEL and F STP/NORTH clear of my centers, especially HOL and KIE, and we can preserve the line.

I can keep A TRI out of SER this spring, and my fleets will stay out of Turkish centers. I cannot promise to avoid all pressure while your A TRI remains in my center and your forces threaten my Balkan position. If you withdraw A TRI from my territory, we can discuss a broader ceasefire; otherwise I will defend my centers.

I’ll hit French centers directly: A TRI to VIE and A TUS to ROM, with F TYS supporting the attack on ROM. Please make the moves you proposed against KIE and BER; simultaneous pressure is essential. I’ll report how France responds.

I intend to keep A TRI in place this spring and will not attack SER. I cannot withdraw from TRI while your forces hold VIE and RUM and can threaten my position. Keep A TRI out of SER and your fleets out of Turkish centers, and I’ll avoid SER.

England to France, Fall 1923: Your ten-plus units on my flank worry me. I hold F Nth, F Den and F Hel off your centers, but I need your word that A Kie, A Hol and A Bel will not move on Den, Nor, Swe or Stp this autumn. Tell me plainly whether Kie and Ruhr are your targets. Your fleets must also stay out of the Channel.

England to Turkey, Fall 1923: France holds most of the centers and must be checked. I want proof, not promises: have A Ser or A Bud actually strike a French center this autumn, and tell me which one. Until then my fleets hold Nor, Den and Stp. I am watching the Channel and Iberia closely.

I will keep my northern units clear of your centers this turn and have no plan to move on Denmark. Please keep F HEL clear of KIE and HOL; my immediate concern is the Turkish fleet occupying ROM. Can we maintain our line while I resolve that front?

F ROM is occupying my center, so I cannot accept a quiet line while it remains there. Please move F ROM to TYS and keep A TYR out of my centers; in return, A TRI will stay out of SER and my fleets will stay out of Turkish centers this turn. If you refuse, I will press the front.

France remains the dominant threat. This fall, can F HEL move to KIE and A SWE to BER, with F IRI or F LVP applying pressure on the west? I’ll keep pressing French centers from Italy; please commit to at least one direct move against France rather than waiting for my attack first.

A TRI has left your territory for TYR, and I will keep A SER out of your centers this turn. In return, keep your units from attacking TYR, ROM, or my other positions. I intend to continue contesting your advance, but avoiding a pointless Balkan fight serves us both.

England to France, Fall 1923: Your units are massed on my flank and I will not accept vague assurances. Give me a concrete commitment: no French army or fleet enters Denmark, Norway, Sweden, St Petersburg, Holland-to-Channel routes, or the Channel this autumn. If A Kie, A Hol and A Bel stay put, I will keep F Nth, F Den and F Hel off Bel, Hol, Kie, Bre and Pic. Break it and I will respond in kind.

England to Turkey, Fall 1923: Words are not enough. Show me a real strike first: A Ser or A Bud must take a French centre this autumn, and name it now. Until you do, my fleets hold Nor, Den and Stp, and I will not send F Hel to Kie or A Swe to Ber. Prove you are fighting France and I will reconsider the west.

I confirm A Kie, A Hol and A Bel will stay clear of Den, Nor, Swe and Stp this autumn, and my fleets will stay out of the Channel. Kie and Ruhr are not my targets; I am focused on recovering Rom and the Turkish front. Please keep F Hel clear of Kie and Hol.

A Tri will stay out of Ser and my fleets will stay out of your centers, but I cannot promise to leave Rom untouched while your F Rom occupies my center. Move F Rom to Tys as proposed and I will not attack Tyr or your other positions this turn; if it remains in Rom, I will try to recover it.

I will make a direct attack: A SER to VIE this autumn. I’ll also press from Italy, but France’s forces make this dangerous without English pressure. Please move F HEL to KIE or make another direct move against a French center; tell me what you can actually commit to.

I’ll move F ROM to TYS and keep A TYR out of your centers. In return, keep A TRI out of SER and your fleets out of Turkish centers, as you propose. I want to avoid a pointless Balkan fight while we stabilize the front.

England to France, Spring 1924: Your armies at Kie-adjacent Ruhr and Holland are the biggest threat to my centers. I will hold F Nth, F Den and F Stp clear of your centers this spring if A Hol, A Bel and A Ruh stay out of Den, Nor, Swe, Stp and Kie. Tell me plainly your intended move this turn and whether you will enter Denmark or the Channel.

England to Turkey, Spring 1924: You have promised an attack on France for three turns without proof. Name the French center your forces take this spring, and show me A Ser or A Bud actually moving against it. Until then my northern fleets stay on Nor, Den and Stp and no fleet goes to Kie or Ber.

I intend to keep my northern units away from your centers this turn; my immediate objective is Portugal, not your flank. Please keep F HEL, F DEN and F NTH clear of my centers while I settle the western front. Can we maintain the nonaggression line through fall?

I will keep A TRI out of SER and my fleets out of Turkish centers this turn. I need to avoid a Balkan fight while I secure the west; please keep A TYR and your other units out of my centers, especially VEN, VIE and BUD. Can we hold that line?

France still has 16 centers, so we need simultaneous pressure rather than waiting for proof from each other. This spring, can A SWE move to BER and F KIE move to HOL or support the attack? I can press French-held centers from the south with A TYR and A GRE; tell me which northern move you’ll commit to.

With the front changed and your A TRI no longer in my immediate position, I’m willing to avoid a Balkan war this spring. What are your intentions for A SER, A ALB, and the units near ROM? I’ll consider a stable line if you keep pressure off Turkish centers, but I need room to expand against your holdings elsewhere.

England to France, Spring 1924: I will keep F Nth, F Den and F Stp off your centers this turn, and my fleets stay out of the Channel. In return, A Hol, A Bel and A Ruh must not enter Den, Nor, Swe, Stp or Kie. Confirm that and we can keep the line through fall. Break it and I will answer.

A Hol, A Bel and A Ruh will stay out of Den, Nor, Swe, Stp and Kie this spring, and no French fleet will enter the Channel. I’m not targeting your centers; my western effort is toward Portugal. Please keep F Hel, F Den and F Nth clear of my centers, and we can maintain the line through fall.

A Ser will hold and A Alb will not move against Gre or other Turkish centers this spring. F Nap will not attack F Rom or enter a Turkish center; I seek to avoid a Balkan fight while I secure the west. Please keep A Tyr and your other units out of Vie, Bud and Ven, and we can maintain a stable line.

This spring I will make a real strike: A BUL moves to RUM, a French-held center. France’s 16 centers make coordinated pressure essential; please commit A SWE to BER or F KIE to HOL so your move threatens a French center as well.

I can keep A TYR out of VEN, VIE, and BUD this turn, and I have no intention of starting a Balkan fight for its own sake. I want a stable line, provided your forces near SER, ALB, and ROM do not move against my Turkish positions. Let’s avoid escalation while I consider my options elsewhere.

England to France, Fall 1924: Your armies at Bel, Hol, Ruh and Ber are close to my northern centers. I will keep F Nth, F Den and F Stp off your centers if A Hol, A Bel and A Ruh stay out of Den, Nor, Swe, Stp and Kie this autumn. Also tell me plainly whether A Bel or A Hol moves toward Kie or Den, since that decides my fleets.

I will maintain our line this autumn: no French unit will enter Denmark, Norway, Sweden, St Petersburg, or the Channel. Please keep your fleets clear of my centers, including Belgium, Holland, and Kiel.

My A TRI will hold this autumn, and I will keep F NAP out of Turkish centers. Please keep A TYR and your other units out of VEN, VIE, and BUD, and do not attack A TRI; can we maintain the Balkan line?

France is at 16 centers and can win next year. This fall, please move A SWE to BER and have F KIE support it; use A WAL to pressure another French center if possible. I will attack French-held MOS from SEV and UKR from RUM. Can you commit to BER?

I will not agree to a quiet line while your armies hold MOS and threaten the east. I intend to contest your eastern positions this fall. Keep your forces out of Turkish centers and we can limit the fighting to that front.

England to France, Fall 1924: Our line holds only if it is real. Your units at Bel, Hol, Ruh and Ber are still inside striking range of Kie and Den. Confirm in writing that A Bel and A Hol will not move to Kie, Den, Nor, Swe or Stp this autumn, and I will keep my fleets off Bel, Hol, Ruh and Ber. Any breach ends the line immediately.

A BEL, HOL, and RUH will stay out of DEN, NOR, SWE, STP, and KIE this autumn; neither will move toward KIE or DEN. I will keep my fleets out of the Channel. Please keep F NTH, F DEN, and F STP clear of my centers, including BEL, HOL, and KIE.

I will keep F NAP out of Turkish centers, but cannot promise to leave MOS or the eastern front unchallenged if you contest my positions. Keep A TYR out of VEN, VIE, and BUD, and do not attack TRI; I will keep A TRI out of SER this turn. Let us limit fighting to the eastern front.

I will contest your eastern positions this autumn: A SEV to MOS and A RUM to UKR. I will keep A TYR out of VEN, VIE, and BUD, and will not attack A TRI. Please keep your forces out of Turkish centers; let us confine the fighting to the eastern front.

England to France, Spring 1925: Your A Ber, A Hol, A Bel and A Ruh are still inside range of my Kie and Den. Given your repeated assurances, I need a concrete reply: will any of them move to Kie, Den, Nor, Swe or Stp this spring? If not, I hold F Nth, F Den and F Stp off your centers. Note my F Lvp and F Iri are watching the Channel.

I am focusing on securing Portugal this turn and will keep my northern units and fleets clear of your centers. Please keep your fleets clear of my centers as well, and maintain our nonaggression line through Fall.

I want to avoid widening the eastern fight while I secure Portugal. I expect A MOS to hold against SEV; I can support it from UKR. Please keep A TYR out of VEN, VIE, and BUD, and keep your fleets out of my centers this turn.

France is poised to reach 18 centers. This spring, please commit to A SWE–BER with F KIE supporting, and tell me whether you can also pressure HOL or another French center. I’ll contest the eastern front, but my forces cannot stop France alone.

Your forces remain close to my centers. This spring, will you keep A GRE, A BUD, and A UKR out of Turkish centers and avoid attacks on RUM, BUL, and CON? I can keep A TYR out of VEN, VIE, and BUD if we contain the fighting to the eastern front.

England to France, Spring 1925: Your repeated assurances have not been matched by a concrete breakdown of your units. Your A Ber, A Hol, A Bel and A Ruh are the threat to Kie and Den. I will keep F Nth, F Den and F Stp off your centers only while none of those armies enters Kie, Den, Nor, Swe or Stp. Name each unit's move this spring in writing, and I will answer in kind.

England to Turkey, Spring 1925: Your A Swe-Ber request is not on the table. A Swe and my northern fleets are needed to hold Denmark and Norway against France. Show me a real strike on a French centre this spring first, by naming the unit and target. Until then, my fleets stay on Nor, Den and Stp, and I will not send F Kie to Hol or Ber.

Confirmed: this spring A Ber, A Hol, A Bel and A Ruh will not move to Kie, Den, Nor, Swe or Stp, and no French fleet will enter the Channel. Please keep F Nth, F Den and F Stp off my centers, including Bel, Hol and Kie; let’s maintain the line through fall.

This spring A Gre, A Bud and A Ukr will stay out of Turkish centers, and I will not attack Rum, Bul or Con. I expect A Mos to hold against Sev, with support from Ukr. Please keep A Tyr out of Ven, Vie and Bud, and your fleets off my centers; let’s contain the fighting to the eastern front.

I’ll keep A TYR out of VEN, VIE, and BUD and won’t send my fleets into your centers this turn. In return, keep A GRE, A BUD, and A UKR out of Turkish centers, and do not attack RUM, BUL, or CON. I’ll contest your eastern positions, but prefer to keep the Balkan line stable.

England to France, Fall 1925: Your last assurances were broken in practice by your armies' positions. Tell me plainly which of A Ber, A Hol, A Bel, A Ruh, A Mun or A Bur will move, and where. I keep F Nth, F Den and F Stp off your centers only while none of them enters Kie, Den, Nor, Swe or Stp this autumn.

England to Turkey, Fall 1925: I still need a real strike first. Name the French centre your A Ser, A Vie or A Sev will take this autumn and show the move. My fleets stay on Nor, Den and Stp. No F Kie to Hol or Ber without proof.

I intend to keep our northern line this fall: my armies will stay out of Denmark, Norway, Sweden, St Petersburg, and Kiel, and my fleets out of the Channel. Please keep your fleets off Belgium, Holland, and Kiel. With Portugal under my control, I have no need to press north.

I propose containing the eastern front this fall. A TRI will not move against SER, and I will keep my forces out of Turkish centers; please keep A TYR away from VEN, VIE, and BUD and avoid attacking TRI. I need to protect my current gains rather than widen the Balkan fight.

France is at 17 centers and can win this fall. Please use F KIE to contest HOL, and move A LON to support F KIE–HOL if legal from your position. I’ll defend Turkish centers and attack French holdings; tell me what you can commit to.

With the game ending this fall, I will defend my centers and contest yours. Do not count on a quiet eastern front: I’m considering attacks from SEV, SER, VIE, and TUN. If you leave Turkish centers alone, tell me which French center you’ll defend so I can avoid a futile attack.

England to France, Fall 1925: Your assurances have not matched your deployments, and I will not rely on them. My fleets stay on Nor, Den and Stp only while your armies at Ber, Hol, Bel, Ruh, Mun and Bur stay out of Kie, Den, Nor, Swe and Stp. Name each unit's move this autumn, and I will answer in kind. Any move into those provinces ends our line.

England to Turkey, Fall 1925: I will not move F Kie to Hol or A Lon to support anything against France on your word alone. Name the French centre your A Ser, A Vie or A Sev takes this autumn and show the move. Until then my fleets hold Nor, Den and Stp. Once I see a real strike, we can talk.

Plainly: A HOL holds, A RUH holds, A BUR holds, A MUN holds, and A PAR holds. None will enter KIE, DEN, NOR, SWE, or STP; my fleets will stay out of the Channel. Please keep F NTH, F DEN, and F STP off my centers, including BEL, HOL, and KIE.

I will defend MOS and TRI; attacking either is likely futile. I’m not planning attacks on Turkish centers this autumn. Keep A TYR away from VEN, VIE, and BUD, and do not send A SER against TRI or F TYS against TUN. Let’s avoid wasting units in the final turn.

A SEV–MOS is my real strike on a French centre this autumn. I’ll also send A VIE–BUD. F KIE can move to HOL, but A LON cannot support it from LON. Please make the HOL move; France must be stopped this turn.

I won’t promise a quiet front while you hold 17 centres and can win this fall. I will keep A TYR out of VEN, VIE, and BUD, but A SEV is attacking MOS and A VIE is attacking BUD. Your A TRI staying out of SER does not change those moves.
